title: Fuel the Liver Ships
endLine: Even-chain fat makes no net glucose, so the liver ships ketones.

scenes.tts: Fat comes apart two carbons at a time, as acetyl coenzyme A. Now stretch that over a long fast. In nineteen sixty-five, Angus Barbieri stopped eating for three hundred eighty-two days. How did his brain keep running?
scenes.narration: Fat comes apart two carbons at a time, as acetyl-CoA. Now stretch that over a long fast. In 1965, Angus Barbieri stopped eating for 382 days. How did his brain keep running?
scenes.caption: Fat comes apart two carbons at a time, as acetyl-CoA. Now stretch that over a long fast. In 1965, Angus Barbieri stopped eating for 382 days. How did his brain keep running?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and COLOUR MAP without a reset: BLUE fatty-acid chain tiles; ORANGE coenzyme A handles; YELLOW attention cues; PINK carriers (FADH2, NADH); GREEN acetyl-CoA carts and ATP earned; RED activation cost and the blood-lane rails; PURPLE workshop wheel; GREY membranes and structure; GOLD the 106 total. New in this film: TEAL capsules are ketone bodies (the first film's drifting TEAL specks become dim GREY so TEAL means only ketones); WHITE hexagon tokens are glucose. A small 'schematic' tag sits bottom right all film. OPEN on the first film's mitochondrial workshop: the 16-tile BLUE chain circles the PURPLE wheel and eight GREEN acetyl-CoA carts roll out, two blocks each, while the GOLD gauge reads 'roughly 106 ATP' (link-back). On 'stretch that over a long fast', the camera pulls back fast: the whole workshop shrinks into a large GREY-outlined cell labelled 'liver' at LEFT (about 40% of the frame, 70% of its height). Two RED rails, the same blood lane as the first film, run from the liver to the RIGHT. At top right a large TEXT-coloured brain outline appears and dims; a plain generic human silhouette (no likeness) stands faintly behind the scene. On '1965', a large day counter at top centre labelled 'days without food' starts ticking from 1. On the question, the counter races to 382 and stops, the brain flickers, and white text fills the top: 'How did the brain keep running?'

Title 'Fuel the Liver Ships' fades in for 2 s over the carried world while the question text fades out. The PURPLE wheel inside the liver keeps turning; the brain outline pulses faintly; the day counter rests at 382.

scenes.tts: Under medical supervision, he lived on water, tea and coffee, with vitamins. He went from four hundred fifty-six pounds to one hundred eighty. Early in a fast, the brain depends on glucose. So where could glucose come from?
scenes.narration: Under medical supervision, he lived on water, tea and coffee, with vitamins. He went from 456 pounds to 180. Early in a fast, the brain depends on glucose. So where could glucose come from?
scenes.caption: Under medical supervision, he lived on water, tea and coffee, with vitamins. He went from 456 pounds to 180. Early in a fast, the brain depends on glucose. So where could glucose come from?
scenes.visual: Same world. The day counter resets to 1. On 'water, tea and coffee', three small cup icons appear under the counter. On the weights, a large BLUE fat droplet, drawn inside the faint silhouette, shrinks steadily as the counter runs again to 382; a weight readout beside it rolls from '456 lb' down to '180 lb' (droplet area scaled from these two values; path between them schematic). On 'the brain depends on glucose', WHITE hexagon tokens travel along the RED blood lane into the brain outline, which brightens. On the final question, the hexagon stream thins to a trickle and a white question mark sits on the empty blood lane.

scenes.tts: Not from even-chain fat, by the usual route. Each turn of the citric acid cycle takes in two carbons as acetyl coenzyme A. It loses two as carbon dioxide. No oxaloacetate is left over to build glucose.
scenes.narration: Not from even-chain fat, by the usual route. Each turn of the citric acid cycle takes in two carbons as acetyl-CoA. It loses two as carbon dioxide. No oxaloacetate is left over to build glucose.
scenes.caption: Not from even-chain fat, by the usual route. Each turn of the citric acid cycle takes in two carbons as acetyl-CoA. It loses two as carbon dioxide. No oxaloacetate is left over to build glucose.
scenes.visual: Camera eases into the liver cell; it fills about 70% of the frame. Beside the PURPLE wheel, a GREEN ring labelled 'citric acid cycle' turns. On 'takes in two carbons', one GREEN acetyl-CoA cart drops two BLUE carbon tiles into the ring. On 'loses two', two GREY puffs labelled 'CO2' leave the ring and drift off. A tally under the ring reads 'in: 2 C' then 'out: 2 C', then 'net: 0'. On 'No oxaloacetate is left over', an exit arrow from the ring labelled 'to glucose' stays empty; a WHITE hexagon outline at its tip stays hollow. The ring keeps turning throughout.

scenes.tts: Only the glycerol backbone and the tail of odd chains make net sugar from fat. Most of fat's carbon needs another route.
scenes.narration: Only the glycerol backbone and the tail of odd chains make net sugar from fat. Most of fat's carbon needs another route.
scenes.caption: Only the glycerol backbone and the tail of odd chains make net sugar from fat. Most of fat's carbon needs another route.
scenes.visual: Same liver view. On 'glycerol backbone', a small GREY 'glycerol' token slides into the liver and becomes one WHITE hexagon that leaves on the blood lane toward the brain. On 'the tail of odd chains', a short BLUE three-tile stub labelled 'odd-chain tail' enters and also yields one WHITE hexagon (token counts schematic). On 'another route', the hollow 'to glucose' arrow from the even-chain ring dims and a large YELLOW cue circles the pile of GREEN acetyl-CoA carts building up beside the wheel.

scenes.tts: When glucose is scarce, low insulin floods the liver with fatty acids. It opens the carnitine gate. Beta oxidation then makes acetyl coenzyme A faster than the liver's citric acid cycle can burn it.
scenes.narration: When glucose is scarce, low insulin floods the liver with fatty acids. It opens the carnitine gate. β-oxidation then makes acetyl-CoA faster than the liver's citric acid cycle can burn it.
scenes.caption: When glucose is scarce, low insulin floods the liver with fatty acids. It opens the carnitine gate. β-oxidation then makes acetyl-CoA faster than the liver's citric acid cycle can burn it.
scenes.visual: A small 'insulin' gauge on the liver's edge drops to 'low'. Many BLUE chains stream in along the blood lane into the liver. On 'carnitine gate', a YELLOW gate on the GREY mitochondrial edge (the first film's carnitine colour) swings open and chains pour through to the PURPLE wheel, which spins faster. GREEN acetyl-CoA carts leave the wheel at a high rate; the GREEN citric acid cycle ring takes them in at a slower, fixed rate. A queue of GREEN carts piles up between wheel and ring, growing taller, labelled 'surplus'. Rates are schematic.

scenes.tts: The liver repackages the surplus. Two acetyl coenzyme A become one acetoacetate, a ketone body. It can be reduced to D three hydroxybutyrate, the dominant form in blood.
scenes.narration: The liver repackages the surplus. Two acetyl-CoA become one acetoacetate, a ketone body. It can be reduced to D-3-hydroxybutyrate, the dominant form in blood.
scenes.caption: The liver repackages the surplus. Two acetyl-CoA become one acetoacetate, a ketone body. It can be reduced to D-3-hydroxybutyrate, the dominant form in blood.
scenes.visual: The surplus queue of GREEN carts feeds a small press beside the wheel. On 'Two acetyl coenzyme A become one', two GREEN carts merge into one TEAL capsule labelled 'acetoacetate'; their ORANGE CoA handles drop off and return to the wheel. On 'reduced', a PINK NADH token docks on a TEAL capsule, turns to plain PINK 'NAD+' and leaves; the capsule relabels 'D-3-hydroxybutyrate'. TEAL capsules line up at the liver's edge. Block cartoon only; no molecular structures.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea. Even-chain fat cannot become net glucose. So in a fast, the liver ships fat's two-carbon units as ketone bodies, fuel for other tissues.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea. Even-chain fat cannot become net glucose. So in a fast, the liver ships fat's two-carbon units as ketone bodies, fuel for other tissues.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea. Even-chain fat cannot become net glucose. So in a fast, the liver ships fat's two-carbon units as ketone bodies, fuel for other tissues.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: liver at LEFT, RED blood lane across the middle, tissues at RIGHT. On 'cannot become glucose', the hollow WHITE hexagon outline at the liver flashes once and fades. On 'ships', a steady stream of TEAL capsules leaves the liver along the blood lane. Three tissue icons settle on the right in a column: the brain outline at top, a combined 'heart, muscle, kidney' icon in the middle, and a RED disc labelled 'red blood cell' at bottom. Capsules flow toward all three; none has entered yet. Label under the lane: 'ships ketones'.

scenes.tts: Shipping costs the liver. If it exports palmitate as four acetoacetate, it keeps about twenty-six of the hundred six A T P. The tissues that burn the ketones collect most of the rest.
scenes.narration: Shipping costs the liver. If it exports palmitate as four acetoacetate, it keeps about 26 of the 106 ATP. The tissues that burn the ketones collect most of the rest.
scenes.caption: Shipping costs the liver. If it exports palmitate as four acetoacetate, it keeps about 26 of the 106 ATP. The tissues that burn the ketones collect most of the rest.
scenes.visual: The first film's GOLD gauge returns beside the liver, full at 'roughly 106 ATP'. On 'four acetoacetate', four TEAL capsules (each holding two GREEN blocks, eight in all) line up at the liver's edge. On 'about twenty-six', the gauge splits into two segments drawn to scale from the lesson's numbers: a lower GREEN segment of 26 out of 106, labelled 'liver keeps 26', stays at the liver; the upper segment slides off along the blood lane with the capsules, labelled 'tissues: most of rest' with no number. The liver's PINK carrier tokens stay put while the GREEN blocks ride away inside the capsules.

scenes.tts: Those capsules still hold most of the energy, and the liver made every one. Will the liver burn its own ketones?
scenes.narration: Those capsules still hold most of the energy, and the liver made every one. Will the liver burn its own ketones?
scenes.caption: Those capsules still hold most of the energy, and the liver made every one. Will the liver burn its own ketones?
scenes.visual: A few TEAL capsules drift back toward the liver's own GREEN citric acid cycle ring and hover at its rim. The other tissues stay dim. Question card at top in white: 'Will the liver burn them?' The capsules bob slightly; nothing enters the ring.
Predict pause. The question card stays. TEAL capsules bob at the rim of the liver's GREEN citric acid cycle ring without entering; the ring turns slowly; blood-lane dots drift. No other change.

scenes.tts: No. The liver lacks thiophorase, the enzyme that reloads acetoacetate onto coenzyme A. Red blood cells cannot use ketones either, having no mitochondria. Heart, muscle, kidney and, after adaptation, the brain run on them.
scenes.narration: No. The liver lacks thiophorase, the enzyme that reloads acetoacetate onto coenzyme A. Red blood cells cannot use ketones either, having no mitochondria. Heart, muscle, kidney and, after adaptation, the brain run on them.
scenes.caption: No. The liver lacks thiophorase, the enzyme that reloads acetoacetate onto coenzyme A. Red blood cells cannot use ketones either, having no mitochondria. Heart, muscle, kidney and, after adaptation, the brain run on them.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves into a white 'No'. On 'thiophorase', an empty ORANGE CoA-handle slot at the entry to the liver's GREEN citric acid cycle ring stays empty, tagged 'no thiophorase'; the hovering capsules bounce off and join the blood-lane stream. On 'Red blood cells', capsules reach the RED disc and bounce off; a tag reads 'no mitochondria'. On 'Heart, muscle, kidney', capsules enter the middle icon, an ORANGE handle clips onto each, it splits into two GREEN blocks, and the icon glows GREEN. On 'after adaptation, the brain', capsules enter the brain outline, which glows GREEN more slowly. Labels: 'cannot use' under liver and red cell; 'can use' under the other two.

scenes.tts: George Cahill's starvation studies measured the payoff. By day forty, protein breakdown fell from roughly seventy-five to twenty grams a day. The brain had shifted onto ketones, sparing muscle.
scenes.narration: George Cahill's starvation studies measured the payoff. By day 40, protein breakdown fell from roughly 75 to 20 grams a day. The brain had shifted onto ketones, sparing muscle.
scenes.caption: George Cahill's starvation studies measured the payoff. By day 40, protein breakdown fell from roughly 75 to 20 grams a day. The brain had shifted onto ketones, sparing muscle.
scenes.visual: The day counter at top runs from 1 to 40. Beside the muscle icon, a vertical bar labelled 'protein broken down (g/day)' starts at 75 and falls to 20 as the counter reaches 40 (end values from the lesson; the path between them schematic). As it falls, the brain outline fills with more TEAL capsules and fewer WHITE hexagons, and the muscle icon slows to a trickle of small GREY protein chips.

scenes.tts: That is how a year of fat could feed a brain. By Cahill's data, Barbieri's brain would have run largely on ketones from his own fat. Gluconeogenesis would have supplied the glucose it still needed.
scenes.narration: That is how a year of fat could feed a brain. By Cahill's data, Barbieri's brain would have run largely on ketones from his own fat. Gluconeogenesis would have supplied the glucose it still needed.
scenes.caption: That is how a year of fat could feed a brain. By Cahill's data, Barbieri's brain would have run largely on ketones from his own fat. Gluconeogenesis would have supplied the glucose it still needed.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world with the faint generic silhouette behind it. The day counter runs again toward 382 while the BLUE fat droplet shrinks and the weight readout rolls from '456 lb' to '180 lb'. A small tag 'would have (not measured)' sits beside the brain. The brain outline is fed by a broad TEAL capsule stream from the liver plus a thin WHITE hexagon trickle labelled 'gluconeogenesis'. Both streams keep flowing as the counter lands on 382.

scenes.tts: The even-chain carbons made no net sugar. The liver turned them into a fuel it cannot burn, and sent it to tissues that can.
scenes.narration: The even-chain carbons made no net sugar. The liver turned them into a fuel it cannot burn, and sent it to tissues that can.
scenes.caption: The even-chain carbons made no net sugar. The liver turned them into a fuel it cannot burn, and sent it to tissues that can.
scenes.visual: On 'never became sugar', the hollow WHITE hexagon outline at the liver flashes once more and fades for good. On 'a fuel it cannot burn', the liver's empty CoA slot glows. On 'tissues that can', the TEAL stream along the blood lane brightens and the brain and the heart-muscle-kidney icon glow GREEN together; the red blood cell stays dim.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (TEAL capsules flowing from liver to brain and muscle, the PURPLE wheel turning). Hex waves above the line. Large centred white text: 'Even-chain fat makes no net glucose, so the liver ships ketones.' No title repeated.
